name: PCF8575 16-bit I/O expander
description: TI 16-bit quasi-bidirectional I/O expander for I2C (up to 400 kHz): every transfer is a byte pair, port 0 (P07..P00) then port 1 (P17..P10); no registers, no direction register. A pin latched high is a weak 30-300 uA pull-up that can be read as an input; latched low it sinks up to 25 mA, so drive LEDs active-low from VCC. Chip supply 2.5-5.5 V, I2C address 0x20-0x27 (0100 A2 A1 A0). Sold as: Adafruit PCF8575 I2C 16 GPIO Expander Breakout (#5611); pins labelled P0-P7 = chip P00-P07 and P8, P9, 10-15 = chip P10-P17. Modelled as one 26-pin row: bottom header VIN, G, SCL, SDA, P0-P7, then top header IRQ, A0, A1, A2, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, P9, P8, then one pad each of the 8-pad VCC (+) and GND (-) rails; STEMMA QT connectors; address 0x20 with A0-A2 open.
eli5: Gives your board sixteen extra on/off pins over just two I2C wires, for buttons and LEDs.

supplierQuery: Adafruit PCF8575 I2C 16 GPIO expander breakout 5611
buildNotes: Every transfer is two bytes: first P7..P0 (chip P07..P00), then 15..P8 (chip P17..P10). Always write and read an even number of bytes.
A pin can only pull high weakly (30-300 uA). Wire LEDs from VCC through a resistor (e.g. 1 k) into the pin so they light when the pin is written 0.
To use a pin as an input, write it 1 first (all pins are 1 at power-on), then wire the button from the pin to GND: pressed reads 0.
Address 0x20 by default; tie A0/A1/A2 to VIN or close the jumpers on the back for 0x21-0x27 (up to 8 boards on one bus).
Never drive a pin that is written 0 high from outside: it sinks a large current to GND (25 mA rated per pin).
The VCC and GND rows are 8 pads each on the same nets as VIN and G; only one of each is modelled.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from pcf8575 import PCF8575

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=400000)
io = PCF8575(i2c, 0x20)
# Button from pin 15 (chip P17) to GND; LED + 1 k resistor from VCC to P0 (lights when P0 is pulled low).
while True:
    pressed = io.pin(15) == 0     # pin 15 stays latched high, so it reads the button
    io.pin(0, 0 if pressed else 1)
    print('BUTTON=%s LED=%s PORT=%04X' % ('PRESSED' if pressed else 'RELEASED', 'ON' if pressed else 'OFF', io.read_port()))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
